question: The proposal for a future-proof design of electricity bills sets minimum targets for the roll-out of smart meters. According to the Commission’s strategic roadmap for digitalisation and AI in the energy sector, accelerating this roll-out is a key measure for the integration of renewable energy. However, the term ‘smart meter’ is not used uniformly across the EU.

It encompasses both simple, remotely readable electricity meters, and intelligent metering systems with secure communication infrastructure and control functions for grid-optimised management. Classifying them uniformly as ‘smart meters’ does not adequately reflect their contributions to the digitalisation and flexibility of the energy system. 1.

Does the Commission share the view that metering systems with different technical capabilities make varying contributions to the digitalisation of the energy system, the integration of renewable energy, the activation of flexibility, and grid-optimised control?
Does the Commission consider it appropriate to establish an EU-wide harmonised system that makes a greater contribution to the digitalisation of energy systems and grid-optimised control?

What measures will the Commission take to reduce regulatory differences – particularly regarding the requirements for the approval and deployment of smart metering systems – and to promote cross-border competition and the widespread adoption of interoperable smart metering systems?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (27.11.2026) Directive (EU) 2019/9441 provides a common definition of a smart metering system and sets out, in Article 20, the functionalities that such systems must provide. These include access to actual time-of-use and near real-time data, secure data communication and the ability to support demand response and other services.

Different technical implementations may provide additional capabilities, but systems deployed under the Directive must comply with these common requirements. The EU framework already establishes common minimum functional requirements, while allowing flexibility in the technical implementation of smart metering systems.
The Commission considers that convergence should focus on ensuring common functionalities, interoperability and standards, rather than prescribing a single technical architecture.

The Commission proposal on future-proofing electricity bills2 reinforces this approach: smart metering systems counting towards the proposed 50 % and 75 % deployment targets must meet the functional requirements of Article 20 of Directive (EU) 2019/944. The Commission will continue supporting interoperability and consistent implementation of the EU framework.

Directive (EU) 2019/944 requires smart metering systems to be deployed in accordance with European standards and establishes requirements on data access, security and interoperability. In addition, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/11623 establishes common interoperability requirements and procedures for access to metering and consumption data.
The Commission proposal on future-proofing electricity bills2 complements these measures by accelerating the smart metering deployment meeting the common EU functionality requirements.
1 Directive (EU) 2019/944 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 June 2019 on common rules for
the internal market for electricity and amending Directive 2012/27/EU (recast), OJ L 158, 14.6.2019, pp. 125– 199, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/944/oj.

2 Proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2019/943, as regards future-proofing electricity bills in the Union, through reducing system costs and fostering electrification and digitalisation (COM/2026/600 final), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52026PC0600&qid=1784719441095.

3 Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2023/1162 of 6 June 2023 on interoperability requirements and non-discriminatory and transparent procedures for access to metering and consumption data, OJ L 154, 15.6.2023, pp. 10–40, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2023/1162/oj.
